text: In nineteen oh two, a city paid people to kill rats. And ended up with more rats than ever.
This is Hanoi, then a French colony. The French built a brand new quarter, with modern sewers.
The sewers turned out to be a perfect highway for rats. Straight into the fanciest houses in town.
And with plague spreading across Asia, rats were the last thing anyone wanted.
So the city hired workers to go down into the sewers, and paid them for every rat.
It worked. On June the twelfth alone, they killed over twenty thousand rats.
But counting dead rats was disgusting. So the city made it simple: just bring us the tail. One cent per tail.
Then the officials noticed something strange. Rats, all over the city... with no tails.
The hunters were catching rats, cutting off the tails, and letting them go. So they could make more rats.
Inspectors even found people outside the city... breeding rats. For their tails.
The bounty was cancelled. The rats stayed. And the plague came anyway.
Economists have a name for this: the cobra effect. Pay people for a problem, and you get more of the problem.
Hanoi wanted to get rid of its rats. Instead, it started the rat business.
